name: Whitcombe City

location.about: A shipbuilding city of about 300,000 at the mouth of the River Whit in the North East. The yards closed in the 1980s and the city had hard years; now there's a university, a car plant, wind-farm work in the old docks - and, since 2017, a football club with some of the richest owners in the world.

colours.story: Sea green and navy - the green of the North Sea off the harbour, and the navy of the shipwrights' overalls. The founders, apprentices at the Whit yards, chose them in 1877.

home.shirt: sea green with a navy collar

third.shirt: white with thin navy and green hoops

rivals.why: the seaside town twelve miles up the coast - yards against pits, played since 1881
the title race of the 2020s - Whitcombe won it in 2021 and 2025, Eastvale in 2023, and Eastvale won the 2026 League Cup final

history.title: The shipwrights
history.text: Founded in 1877 by apprentices at the Whit shipyards. The Association Cup in 1881, the Second Division in its first season (1893), champions in 1899 and 1903, and the cup again in 1902 and 1912.

history.title: Cup city
history.text: The Association Cup in 1927, 1938 and 1949; relegated in the twenties and back as Second Division champions in 1930; champions in 1933 and 1939. Down again in the fifties - and back up as champions in 1959.

history.title: The Shield
history.text: The Association Cup in 1961, the League Cup in 1967, 1973 and 1984 - and the club's only European trophies, the Continental Shield in 1978 and 1986. Relegated in 1970 and straight back up in 1971; the cup again in 1983 as the yards closed around them.

history.title: One last title, then the slide
history.text: Champions in 1998 under Geordie Laidlaw, second in 2008 - then debts, a ground falling apart, and relegation in 2014. They came back up as runners-up in 2016.

history.title: The new money
history.text: An overseas investment fund bought the club in 2017. The title in 2021 - the first in twenty-three years - and again in 2025 and 2026, back-to-back champions. The League Cup still won't come: finals lost in 2019, 2024 and 2026.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1899 = 1898-99).

legends.name: Geordie Laidlaw
legends.note: The 1998 title. The Laidlaw Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Jack 'Rivets' Robson
legends.note: 309 goals - the club record, and both titles of the thirties.

legends.name: Stan Cuthbertson
legends.note: Both Continental Shields, the 1983 cup and two League Cups.

legends.name: Jordan Akintola
legends.note: The star of the 2021, 2025 and 2026 champions.

records.attendance: 75,118 v Sandmere Athletic, League, 1949 (Tollgate Park, before seating)

badge.about: The ship on the river for the yards that made the city; the castle tower for the old city wall; sea green and navy. Motto 'Per Mare Ad Gloriam' - by the sea to glory.
badge.design: A navy shield with a sea-green border. In the centre a white sailing ship in full sail on three wavy sea-green lines. Above the ship a small white castle tower. 'WHITCOMBE CITY' arched above the shield in navy capitals, and a sea-green ribbon beneath reading 'PER MARE AD GLORIAM' in navy, with '1877' on the ribbon's ends.

ground.name: Tollgate Park

stands.name: Laidlaw Stand
stands.roof: a big cantilever, high above the pitch
stands.features: the main stand, towering over the city: tunnel, dugouts, boxes, the directors' box

stands.name: Yard End
stands.features: the home end, two tiers of sea-green seats; the shipyard cranes kept as monuments behind it

stands.name: Harbour Stand
stands.roof: a new roof with glass panels
stands.features: rebuilt by the new owners: hospitality, a club shop, views of the harbour from the back

stands.name: Town End
stands.features: a single tier, away fans in one corner - the owners plan to rebuild it with a second tier

ground.corners: the western corners filled; the north-east corner open
ground.roof: lop-sided - the Laidlaw Stand much higher than the rest
ground.surroundings: right in the city centre on a hill: the river mouth, the harbour and two old shipyard cranes below, terraced streets and the castle walls behind
ground.atmosphere: fierce and proud - the city waited twenty-three years for a title and it shows
